newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain would mobilise world for Hong Kong - Patten.
newsitem.headline: Britain would mobilise world for Hong Kong - Patten.

text.p: Governor Chris Patten said on Thursday Britain would mobilise international support to press Beijing into keeping its treaty promises regarding Hong Kong if problems surfaced after the British pull out next year.

"If there are problems...they (British leaders) would want to mobilise as much international support as possible to persuade China to keep its word under the Joint Declaration," Patten told a caller on a Hong Kong radio phone-in.

The Joint Declaration is the 1984 Sino-British treaty, registered at the United Nations, setting out the framework for China to take back Hong Kong at midnight next June 30 after more than a century and a half of British rule.

"Britain has a continuing moral commitment to Hong Kong because we're one of the signatories to the Joint Declaration and it is equally the case the whole international community will be watching what happens here with great interest," Patten said.

He was fielding questions from the public about his final annual policy speech, in which he vigorously defended Hong Kong's fledgling democracy and human rights set-up and warned that China's plans to erase them would cause instability.
Some callers voiced concerns about a provisional legislature that China plans to install after it scraps the present elected chamber.
In Wednesday's policy speech Patten, the 28th and last British governor, attacked the provisional legislature plan and and urged Beijing to reconsider it.
"There are very few things which could give people more confidence about the future than a commitment to allow the freely elected legislature to go through to the end of its four-year term," he said.
